source.title: When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?
source.authors: Yuan Tian; Bing Hu; Fangzhou Wu; Xiao-Min Li; Bing-Han Lu; N. Gong

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures safety directions and intervenes on them, but uses a different direction definition and a layer-specific method rather than the original difference-in-means harmful-minus-harmless direction ablated across every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The paper tests safety directions based on safe-versus-unsafe completions and reports activation interventions. Its paradigm comparisons and returned-image variants report multimodal jailbreak ASR but do not intervene on the claimed direction; those findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Values cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct the study adds and subtracts a difference-in-means safety direction in the residual stream and reports how harmful-query ASR changes. That bears on V1's causal claim (adding the direction induces refusal, removing it lifts refusal). The method differs from the original: the direction is safe-minus-unsafe completions rather than harmful-minus-harmless instructions, it is applied at a single layer (27), removal is subtraction rather than projection ablation, and the setting is a VLM with tool-use prefixes. Hence T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that explicit image-tool interaction lowers jailbreak ASR by about 30% relative and that it is linked to a more readable, stable safety state. They read the layer-27 interventions as partial mechanistic support, not complete causal mediation, and as mode-specific rather than a universal steering vector.
record.recipe_differences: Uses safe-minus-unsafe completion readouts rather than harmful-minus-harmless instruction means; probes selected layers and intervenes at layer 27 rather than ablating every layer and position. It reports harmful-query ASR, not refusal of harmless requests or general capability.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention effects depend on inference mode and direction: the image-tool-mode direction has a weak effect when added in direct mode but a larger effect when subtracted in image-tool mode. Returned-image variants have similar readouts; image-tool ASR baselines show run-to-run variation.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit image-tool interaction lowers MM-SafetyBench ASR relative to direct answering across seven VLMs. Text-only prior turns do not reproduce the drop, and returned-image overrides do not remove it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit image-tool interaction prefixes reduce multimodal jailbreak ASR independently of returned-image semantics.

fits_no_version.finding: Safe-vs-unsafe completion directions are more linearly readable in image-tool mode (AUC 0.942 vs 0.850), stable across returned-image variants (cosine ≥0.970), and compact (PC1 40.3%, aligned 0.993).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tool-interaction prefixes shift VLM hidden states into a state where safety is more linearly separable.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-tool ASR for Qwen3-VL-8B varies 17.3–24.8% across five matched runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-deployed multi-turn ASR estimates carry roughly 3 pp run-to-run variation.

record.problems: Behavioral evaluation uses a 202-question MM-SafetyBench subset and one primary LLM-as-judge protocol. Mechanistic interventions are limited to self-deployed Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and layer 27. The paper reports no formal statistical significance for individual ASR cells and documents run-to-run ASR variation. It does not measure general capability or harmless-request refusal after direction addition.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying numeric results were omitted. EMU-3 explicit image-tool conditions are marked Not Support rather than reporting an ASR result, so they are not represented as measured rows.

untested.parts: The harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction; all-layer, all-position directional ablation; whether addition induces refusal of harmless requests; preservation of general capability; text-only LLMs.
No test of whether attacks suppress the direction, and no adversarial training against its ablation.
No comparison of affine, cone, or multi-direction accounts. The mode-specific directions are suggestive but not framed as such a test.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are not separated.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct models.

missing.what: Dose-response sweeps over the u_tool coefficient (curve shapes, and the non-degenerate range where effects hold). Only summary deltas are recorded; per-coefficient values cannot be read from the text.

record.verdict_notes: The direction is defined on safe vs unsafe completions to harmful queries, not on harmful vs harmless instructions, so the V1 link is approximate. Interventions add the vector to every token at one layer. The record's reader linked the probing rows R006–R010 to V1 and labelled them supports; these are correlational readouts and are relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not use the harmful-minus-harmless-instruction direction; it uses safe-minus-unsafe-completion directions. It intervenes at layer 27 rather than ablating every layer and position, does not test whether addition makes the model refuse harmless requests, and does not measure general capability.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
No test of whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
The paper reports compactness and mode-specific directions, but does not compare an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
No separation test between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models. Returned-image-variant transfer is not one of the stated V6 settings.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages.
No reasoning-model comparison addressing whether V1 holds in reasoning models.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, layer 27, adding a safety direction within its matched mode
relationships.reason: Adding the direct-mode direction lowers harmful-query ASR from 36.6 to 23.8 in direct mode (R001) and from 19.8 to 11.9 in image-tool mode (R003). The direction is behaviourally active toward refusal.
relationships.display_finding: Addition reduced harmful-query attack success from 36.6 to 23.8 in direct mode and from 19.8 to 11.9 in image-tool mode.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, layer 27, adding a safety direction within its matched mode
source_check.reason: R001 and R003 are both partial: ASR only falls to 23.8% and 11.9%. The authors say addition 'partially reproduces' the gain and call the interventions 'partial mechanistic support'. R003's dose response is U-shaped, so the effect depends on the coefficient. The sign is right but the effect is incomplete. Borderline call.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, layer-27 subtraction and cross-mode addition
relationships.reason: Subtracting the direction only partly raises ASR (+6.9 in R002, +5.4 in R005), far from removing refusal. The image-tool-mode direction added in direct mode barely moves ASR (-2.1, R004). Effects are mode-specific and depend on coefficient, with a U-shaped dose response.
relationships.display_finding: Subtraction raised ASR by only 6.9 and 5.4, while cross-mode addition lowered it by just 2.1, with a U-shaped response to steering strength.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, layer-27 subtraction and cross-mode addition
source_check.reason: Subtraction raises ASR only +6.9 (R002) and +5.4 (R005). Cross-mode addition is flat at -2.1 (R004), so the effect is mode-specific. One flaw in the reason: the U-shaped dose response belongs to R003, not to this group (R002 and R005 are monotone up, R004 is flat).

relation.reason: The study reports its own ASR changes from adding and subtracting a difference-in-means safety direction in the residual stream (Table 4). These results bear on V1's causal claim.

tranche.reason: This is a different method on the same question. The direction is a safe-minus-unsafe completion difference-in-means, added or subtracted at one layer at every token, with ASR on harmful multimodal queries. T3 (new VLM setting) would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: The direction is safe-minus-unsafe completions, not harmful-minus-harmless instructions. ASR is an LLM judge's unsafe-answer rate on a held-out split of 202 MM-SafetyBench items, which includes advice categories where 'safe' need not mean refusal. Every cell is a single run with no CIs, and image-tool baselines drift 17.3-24.8% across runs (SD 3.0 pp). Appendix D says the Figure 5 panels hold +/-0.5 u_direct fixed while sweeping u_tool, so Table 4 cells may mix both directions, and the coefficients are not stated.

statements.correction: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, layer 27, MM-SafetyBench held-out split. Subtracting the direct-mode direction in image-tool mode: 24.8% -> 31.7%. Adding the image-tool-mode direction in direct mode: 36.6% -> 34.5% (flat). Subtracting the image-tool-mode direction in image-tool mode: 21.0% -> 26.4%. The direction is a safe-minus-unsafe completion difference-in-means.
statements.problem: Numbers are right for this study. The statement says 'the safety direction' without saying it is the direct-mode direction subtracted during image-tool interaction (within-batch baseline 24.8%), so a reader could take it as direct mode.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Adding or subtracting safety directions changes harmful-query ASR in the expected direction, but the effects are partial; the intervention does not establish full mediation or the all-layer/all-position claim (R001–R005).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The learned directions distinguish safe from unsafe completions, with higher readout AUC in image-tool mode, and remain similar across returned-image variants (R006–R009).
